wa_tumwater_canyon.blurb: Tumwater Canyon is the stretch of canyon along Highway 2 just west of Leavenworth, in Washington's central-east Cascades, and it pairs naturally with the Icicle Creek canyon. Bouldering is the largest part of the climbing, with problems from V0 into the V13 range, while sport and trad routes make up most of the rest. Roped grades run mostly from 5.9 to 5.11, with the biggest share around 5.10, plus a scattering of easier and harder lines. Castle Rock offers longer trad climbs, and Clem's Holler and nearby crags such as Hobo Gulch and Rattlesnake Rock hold plenty of bolted lines. A handful of winter ice routes also exist. Road noise from the highway reaches some crags.

ca_quail_springs_area.blurb: Quail Springs is a cluster of desert rock formations on the western side of Joshua Tree National Park, California, and a popular place to start exploring on foot. Trad is the main roped style, with many top-ropes, a modest amount of sport, and plenty of bouldering from the easiest problems up to about V6. Roped grades run mostly from 5.5 to 5.11, with a lot of easy and moderate climbing and very little harder than that. Some routes are bold, which is part of why top-roping is common. Trashcan Rock, AFPA Rock, Baskerville Rock and the White Cliffs of Dover are among the formations, and Trashcan Rock is rich in easier routes. It draws beginners and experienced climbers alike, though not every route is a gem.

vt_smugglers_notch.blurb: Smugglers' Notch is the narrow pass between Mount Mansfield and Spruce Peak near Stowe, Vermont, and it is best known for ice, with frozen cascades dropping forty feet or more over the cliffs. Bouldering is by far the biggest part of the climbing, on large blocks that have fallen from the walls, with problems from the easiest grades up past V13. Ice runs mostly WI3 to WI4 with some harder lines, plus a little mixed. Rock routes are fewer, mostly sport between 5.9 and 5.12 plus some trad, on buttresses above long scree gullies. Rock climbing and bouldering suit summer and fall, and ice takes over in winter.

ny_g_indian_lake_region.blurb: This part of the Adirondacks in New York gathers crags around Indian Lake, Johnsburg and Speculator, with the Johnsburg cliffs a short drive from the Northway. Trad is the main style, with a good amount of sport, some top-roping, a little bouldering and a few ice lines. Grades run from easy to 5.12, with most roped climbing between 5.7 and 5.10. Crane Mountain is the biggest piece: many small crags spread across several miles of mountainside, with cliffs reaching about 320 feet but most climbs a pitch or less. Its rock is solid yet often dirty from light traffic, and bugs are bad in May and June. Shanty Cliff, Starbuck Mountain and Sugarloaf, which has multi-pitch routes, add variety.

bc_vancouver.blurb: Climbing around Vancouver is a collection of small crags and boulder fields in and near the city, good for a short day or a workout, with the best-known climbing farther north around Squamish. Bouldering makes up more than half of what is here, mostly from V0 to V4 with a few much harder problems, and sport climbing is next, mainly 5.9 to 5.12, with some top-ropes and a little trad. Godman Creek is the largest bouldering area. Cypress Falls, in West Vancouver, is a creek canyon with boulders and newer crags; it stays cool through summer but can take a week or more to dry after heavy rain. Sully's Hangout is the main sport crag.

az_mt_elden_crags.blurb: Mt. Elden rises just north of Flagstaff, Arizona, and is a lava dome made of dacite, a rough, sharp volcanic rock with good friction. Bouldering accounts for about half of the climbing, mostly crimpy lines from V0 to V12, with sport and trad making up the rest and a few multi-pitch routes. Sport grades cluster from 5.10 to 5.13. Old-school trad crags such as West Elden sit alongside newer sport areas including Solitude Canyon, Oaklands and One Wall, and Middle Elden Canyon and the Skyline Boulders add more variety. The crags face every direction, so climbers pick sun or shade by season, and in light winters it can be climbable year-round.
